messages.subject: mqmfind.marker
parts:
Hi all,

I have been using the mqmfind.marker() function to pull out significant marker names and positional information from a MQM type R/qtl object. 

In some cases there are >1 significant QTL per chromosome and the mqmfind.marker() function only returns one marker per chromosome. 

I realize I could just extract all markers above my permutation threshold by subsetting a vector of LOD scores but this returns a lot of MQM pseudomarkers in addition to the actual markers within my genetic map. 

Is there an alternative function or method that you folks prefer to use?

Max

messages.subject: Re: mqmfind.marker
parts:
Alright, I've scripted out a quick and dirty work around. Here it is...

# Get a data frame of all significant markers (pseudomarkers included) with LOD score
sig.markers.pseudo <- out.mqm[out.mqm[,3] > mqm.permutation.threshold,]

# Use the function described below
sig.markers<-get_map_markers_from_mqm(sig.markers.pseudo)


# Here is the definition of the function

get_map_markers_from_mqm<-function(marker_list) {
  # Remove all pseudomarkers (c.#.loc#) to get just markers from map
  map_markers<-marker_list[grep('c[1:9]..*', as.character(marker_list[,1]), invert=T),]
  # Get a list of chromosomes to iterate through
  chrs<-sort(unique(map_markers$chr))
  # Construct a variable to store Markers found at peaks
  peaks<-c()
  # Iterate through list of chromosomes 
  for(c in 1:length(chrs)) {
    # Get dataframe from individual chromosome
    temp<-map_markers[map_markers$chr == chrs[c],]
    # Is the first marker a peak?
    if (temp[1,4] > temp[2,4]) {peaks<-rbind(peaks, temp[1,])}
    # Is the last marker a peak?
    if (temp[nrow(temp),4] > temp[nrow(temp),4]) {peaks<-rbind(peaks, temp[nrow(temp),])}
    # Iterate through each marker and check if current marker's LOD score is greater than the LOD of two markers on either side
    for(r in 2:(nrow(temp)-1)) {
      # Check if value is actually a peak (get LOD left, middle and right)
      lod.l<-temp[r-1,4]
      lod.c<-temp[r,4]
      lod.r<-temp[r+1,4]
      # If marker in the center has higher LOD score than other two markers put into the 'peak' dataframe
      if ((lod.c > lod.l) && (lod.c > lod.r)) {peaks<-rbind(peaks, temp[r,])}
    }
  } 
return(peaks) }
